request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The score's settled figures now leave out corrections: only SETTLED claims that correct nothing
count toward it.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A person's score now counts only SETTLED claims that don't correct another claim. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

I made the change in both places the score is worked out:
- **On screen:** `personScoreOf` in `src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people.ts` now leaves out claims that correct another claim.
- **On the server:** the snapshot in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java` has the same filter. That figure is what the `SCORE` audit record writes when the sheet's today changes.

The person's settled-total column still includes corrections; only the score changed. No stored data or schema needed changing.

After the test run I edited one comment in `RollupService.java` to describe the new rule. It's a comment-only edit, so I didn't run the tests again.
